items.title: 68189_Al Hall oral history interview
items.q: Frankie Newton was the leader, and Sammy Benskon was the pianist and me who worked there for a while.

ctx.x: I thought he was a terrific trumpet player, and we were working opposite bandstands when I was with Billy Hicks. When I was with Billy Hicks, I worked opposite everybody, Tommy Dorsey, Benny Goodman, Chick, Erskine Hawkins, Les Brown, you know, everybody. We were the house group. So we had to fill in the time until they set up, got their instruments together.

But Frankie Newton, I think the last job I worked for him was at a place in the Village called the Little Casino. It was Stella Brooks. It was -- Frankie Newton was the leader, and Sammy Benskon was the pianist and me who worked there for a while.
And all the kids loved him in the Village. He was -- he was the king of the Village. He was giving lessons around, advice to the kids. That's when they would listen.
